slides.text:
A Rust program is a file with a function called `main`: it is where the program starts. Its steps run from top to bottom, and `println!` prints a line. A `use` line above it brings something from the standard library into reach.

The snippet is pseudo code.
First you type the shape of a file and call functions from the standard library. Then you shape text with methods, and finally control how `println!` shows values.

exercises.title: Your first program
exercises.guide: A Rust program is a `main` function. Type one that prints.

chunks.guide: The program starts in `main`.

notes.text: The entry point: the program starts here.

chunks.guide: `println!` prints a line of text.

exercises.title: Mix text and numbers
exercises.guide: Print lines that mix text and numbers.

chunks.guide: Each `{}` takes the next value after the string, in order. Text and numbers can mix; braces can sit between any text.
A value can be a small sum: Rust works it out first.

exercises.title: Borrow from the standard library
exercises.guide: Bring two functions into reach, then call them.

chunks.guide: `use` brings a function from the standard library into reach.

notes.text: Brings something into reach so you can call it by its short name.

chunks.guide: Each function needs its own `use`.

notes.text: The standard library: the code that ships with Rust.
A part of the standard library for comparing values.
A function that gives back the smaller of two values.

chunks.guide: `max` returns the larger of two values.
`min` returns the smaller one.

exercises.title: Make the call work
exercises.guide: The compiler cannot find `min`. Which line, placed above `main`, fixes it?
exercises.explanation: `min` lives in `std::cmp`, so the line names that full path after `use`. `import` is not Rust, and the other paths skip or invent a module.

exercises.title: Skip the shortcut
exercises.guide: No `use` this time: write the full path at each call.

chunks.guide: `::` walks into a module. `std::cmp::min` names the function without a `use`.
The standard library also holds constants, like pi.

notes.text: The decimal number type; here it also names a module.
A module that collects fixed values like pi and e.
The constant pi, with all the precision an f64 holds.

chunks.guide: Paths work inside a sum too.

slides.text:
Text can do things. Write a dot after it, then the method name and brackets. Some methods take a value inside the brackets.

The snippet is pseudo code.

exercises.title: Shout a banner
exercises.guide: Build a title banner out of text methods.

chunks.guide: A method is called with a dot after the text. It returns a new text.

notes.text: Builds a new text by repeating the original.

chunks.guide: Another method changes the letters.

exercises.title: Count the letters
exercises.guide: Ask a text how long it is.

chunks.guide: `len` gives the number of characters.

notes.text: Returns how many characters the text has.

chunks.guide: `to_lowercase` is the opposite of `to_uppercase`.
One method can feed another: the length becomes the repeat count.

exercises.title: Work out the output
exercises.guide: Follow each line. In the options, each `/` is a line break. Pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `"ab".repeat(3)` gives ababab and `to_uppercase` gives RUST. `"-".repeat(2)` is `--` and `"Ana".len()` is 3. `"go".len()` is 2, so `ha` repeats twice.

exercises.title: Fill the method
exercises.guide: The first line must print `*****` and the second `ha!ha!ha!`. Complete both lines.

exercises.title: Escape sequences
exercises.guide: Put special characters inside text, like an order slip.

chunks.guide: A `\n` inside a string starts a new line.

notes.text: Breaks the line at this point.

chunks.guide: A backslash before a double quote keeps it inside the string.

notes.text: The quote is text here, it does not end the string.

chunks.guide: To print one backslash, write two.

output.text:
Order 1042
Status: shipped
Book: "Dune"
Saved to C:\Users\ana

exercises.title: Comment a line out
exercises.guide: Explain a step, and switch a line off.

chunks.guide: Words after `//` are for people. The compiler skips them.

notes.text: Everything after it on the line is ignored.

chunks.guide: Put `//` before code and that line does not run.

slides.text:
Inside the braces you can choose which value goes there, and after a colon how it looks.

The snippet is pseudo code: every part is optional.

exercises.title: Pick by position
exercises.guide: Choose which value each brace shows.

chunks.guide: A number in the braces picks a value by its place in the list, counting from 0.

notes.text: Index 1 is the second value.

chunks.guide: The same number can appear many times, so the value is written once.
Reorder numbers to switch a date from day first to month first.

output.text:
Ana loves Rust
Bye, Bye, Bye!
11/8

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.explanation: `{1}` is the second value, `b`, and `{0}` is the first, `a`. The braces read b, a, b.

exercises.title: Debug format
exercises.guide: Show a user name as the programmer sees it.

chunks.guide: `{}` shows a value the way a person reads it.
`{:?}` shows it as the programmer sees it: strings keep their quotes.

notes.text: The debug form, meant for developers.

chunks.guide: The debug form also escapes special characters, like the quotes of a nickname.

exercises.title: Width and alignment
exercises.guide: Pad the cells of a price table to a fixed width.

chunks.guide: A number after the colon is a minimum width. Text pads on the right by default.

notes.text: The value takes at least 8 characters.

chunks.guide: Align a price to the right edge of the field.

notes.text: Aligns to the right edge of the field.

chunks.guide: Center the price in the field.

notes.text: Centers the value in the field.

exercises.title: Pick the alignment
exercises.guide: Right-align the text on the first line and center it on the second.

chunks.guide: `b` prints a number in binary.

notes.text: Shows the binary digits of the number.

chunks.guide: `x` prints hexadecimal.
`#` adds the `0x` prefix.

notes.text: Adds the base prefix.
